paragraphs.text: Now faith is assurance of [things] hoped for, a conviction of things not seen.
paragraphs.original: Ἔστιν δὲ πίστις ἐλπιζομένων ὑπόστασις, πραγμάτων ἔλεγχος οὐ βλεπομένων·
paragraphs.translit: Estin de pistis elpizomenōn hypostasis, pragmatōn elenchos ou blepomenōn·

paragraphs.text: For therein the elders had witness borne to them.
paragraphs.original: ἐν ταύτῃ γὰρ ἐμαρτυρήθησαν οἱ πρεσβύτεροι.
paragraphs.translit: en tautē gar emartyrēthēsan hoi presbyteroi.

paragraphs.text: By faith we understand that the worlds have been framed by the word of God, so that what is seen hath not been made out of things which appear.
paragraphs.original: πίστει νοοῦμεν κατηρτίσθαι τοὺς αἰῶνας ῥήματι θεοῦ, εἰς τὸ μὴ ἐκ φαινομένων τὸ βλεπόμενον γεγονέναι.
paragraphs.translit: pistei nooumen katērtisthai tous aiōnas rhēmati theou, eis to mē ek phainomenōn to blepomenon gegonenai.

paragraphs.text: By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, through which he had witness borne to him that he was righteous, God bearing witness in respect of his gifts: and through it he being dead yet speaketh.
paragraphs.original: Πίστει πλείονα θυσίαν Ἅβελ παρὰ Κάϊν προσήνεγκεν τῷ θεῷ, διʼ ἧς ἐμαρτυρήθη εἶναι δίκαιος, μαρτυροῦντος ἐπὶ τοῖς δώροις αὐτοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ διʼ αὐτῆς ἀποθανὼν ἔτι λαλεῖ.
paragraphs.translit: Pistei pleiona thysian Habel para Kain prosēnenken tō theō, diʼ hēs emartyrēthē einai dikaios, martyrountos epi tois dōrois autou tou theou, kai diʼ autēs apothanōn eti lalei.

paragraphs.text: By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death; and he was not found, because God translated him: for he hath had witness borne to him that before his translation he had been well-pleasing unto God:
paragraphs.original: Πίστει Ἑνὼχ μετετέθη τοῦ μὴ ἰδεῖν θάνατον, καὶ οὐχ ηὑρίσκετο διότι μετέθηκεν αὐτὸν ὁ θεός· πρὸ γὰρ τῆς μεταθέσεως μεμαρτύρηται εὐαρεστηκέναι τῷ θεῷ,
paragraphs.translit: Pistei Henōch metetethē tou mē idein thanaton, kai ouch hēurisketo dioti metethēken auton ho theos· pro gar tēs metatheseōs memartyrētai euarestēkenai tō theō,

paragraphs.text: And without faith it is impossible to be well-pleasing [unto him]; for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and [that] he is a rewarder of them that seek after him.
paragraphs.original: χωρὶς δὲ πίστεως ἀδύνατον εὐαρεστῆσαι, πιστεῦσαι γὰρ δεῖ τὸν προσερχόμενον τῷ θεῷ ὅτι ἔστιν καὶ τοῖς ἐκζητοῦσιν αὐτὸν μισθαποδότης γίνεται.
paragraphs.translit: chōris de pisteōs adynaton euarestēsai, pisteusai gar dei ton proserchomenon tō theō hoti estin kai tois ekzētousin auton misthapodotēs ginetai.

paragraphs.text: By faith Noah, being warned [of God] concerning things not seen as yet, moved with godly fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house; through which he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is according to faith.
paragraphs.original: πίστει χρηματισθεὶς Νῶε περὶ τῶν μηδέπω βλεπομένων εὐλαβηθεὶς κατεσκεύασεν κιβωτὸν εἰς σωτηρίαν τοῦ οἴκου αὐτοῦ, διʼ ἧς κατέκρινεν τὸν κόσμον, καὶ τῆς κατὰ πίστιν δικαιοσύνης ἐγένετο κληρονόμος.
paragraphs.translit: pistei chrēmatistheis Nōe peri tōn mēdepō blepomenōn eulabētheis kateskeuasen kibōton eis sōtērian tou oikou autou, diʼ hēs katekrinen ton kosmon, kai tēs kata pistin dikaiosynēs egeneto klēronomos.

paragraphs.text: By faith Abraham, when he was called, obeyed to go out unto a place which he was to receive for an inheritance; and he went out, not knowing whither he went.
paragraphs.original: Πίστει καλούμενος Ἀβραὰμ ὑπήκουσεν ἐξελθεῖν εἰς τόπον ὃν ἤμελλεν λαμβάνειν εἰς κληρονομίαν, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν μὴ ἐπιστάμενος ποῦ ἔρχεται.
paragraphs.translit: Pistei kaloumenos Abraam hypēkousen exelthein eis topon hon ēmellen lambanein eis klēronomian, kai exēlthen mē epistamenos pou erchetai.

paragraphs.text: By faith he became a sojourner in the land of promise, as in a [land] not his own, dwelling in tents, with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise:
paragraphs.original: πίστει παρῴκησεν εἰς γῆν τῆς ἐπαγγελίας ὡς ἀλλοτρίαν, ἐν σκηναῖς κατοικήσας μετὰ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ Ἰακὼβ τῶν συγκληρονόμων τῆς ἐπαγγελίας τῆς αὐτῆς·
paragraphs.translit: pistei parōkēsen eis gēn tēs epangelias hōs allotrian, en skēnais katoikēsas meta Isaak kai Iakōb tōn synklēronomōn tēs epangelias tēs autēs·

paragraphs.text: for he looked for the city which hath the foundations, whose builder and maker is God.
paragraphs.original: ἐξεδέχετο γὰρ τὴν τοὺς θεμελίους ἔχουσαν πόλιν, ἧς τεχνίτης καὶ δημιουργὸς ὁ θεός.
paragraphs.translit: exedecheto gar tēn tous themelious echousan polin, hēs technitēs kai dēmiourgos ho theos.

paragraphs.text: By faith even Sarah herself received power to conceive seed when she was past age, since she counted him faithful who had promised:
paragraphs.original: πίστει καὶ αὐτῇ Σάρρᾳ δύναμιν εἰς καταβολὴν σπέρματος ἔλαβεν καὶ παρὰ καιρὸν ἡλικίας, ἐπεὶ πιστὸν ἡγήσατο τὸν ἐπαγγειλάμενον·
paragraphs.translit: pistei kai autē Sarra dynamin eis katabolēn spermatos elaben kai para kairon hēlikias, epei piston hēgēsato ton epangeilamenon·

paragraphs.text: wherefore also there sprang of one, and him as good as dead, [so many] as the stars of heaven in multitude, and as the sand, which is by the sea-shore, innumerable.
paragraphs.original: διὸ καὶ ἀφʼ ἑνὸς ἐγεννήθησαν, καὶ ταῦτα νενεκρωμένου, καθὼς τὰ ἄστρα τοῦ οὐρανοῦ τῷ πλήθει καὶ ὡς ἡ ἄμμος ἡ παρὰ τὸ χεῖλος τῆς θαλάσσης ἡ ἀναρίθμητος.
paragraphs.translit: dio kai aphʼ henos egennēthēsan, kai tauta nenekrōmenou, kathōs ta astra tou ouranou tō plēthei kai hōs hē ammos hē para to cheilos tēs thalassēs hē anarithmētos.

paragraphs.text: These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them and greeted them from afar, and having confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.
paragraphs.original: Κατὰ πίστιν ἀπέθανον οὗτοι πάντες, μὴ λαβόντες τὰς ἐπαγγελίας, ἀλλὰ πόρρωθεν αὐτὰς ἰδόντες καὶ ἀσπασάμενοι, καὶ ὁμολογήσαντες ὅτι ξένοι καὶ παρεπίδημοί εἰσιν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
paragraphs.translit: Kata pistin apethanon houtoi pantes, mē labontes tas epangelias, alla porrōthen autas idontes kai aspasamenoi, kai homologēsantes hoti xenoi kai parepidēmoi eisin epi tēs gēs.

paragraphs.text: For they that say such things make it manifest that they are seeking after a country of their own.
paragraphs.original: οἱ γὰρ τοιαῦτα λέγοντες ἐμφανίζουσιν ὅτι πατρίδα ἐπιζητοῦσιν.
paragraphs.translit: hoi gar toiauta legontes emphanizousin hoti patrida epizētousin.

paragraphs.text: And if indeed they had been mindful of that [country] from which they went out, they would have had opportunity to return.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἰ μὲν ἐκείνης μνημονεύουσιν ἀφʼ ἧς ἐξέβησαν, εἶχον ἂν καιρὸν ἀνακάμψαι·
paragraphs.translit: kai ei men ekeinēs mnēmoneuousin aphʼ hēs exebēsan, eichon an kairon anakampsai·

paragraphs.text: But now they desire a better [country], that is, a heavenly: wherefore God is not ashamed of them, to be called their God; for he hath prepared for them a city.
paragraphs.original: νῦν δὲ κρείττονος ὀρέγονται, τοῦτʼ ἔστιν ἐπουρανίου. διὸ οὐκ ἐπαισχύνεται αὐτοὺς ὁ θεὸς θεὸς ἐπικαλεῖσθαι αὐτῶν, ἡτοίμασεν γὰρ αὐτοῖς πόλιν.
paragraphs.translit: nyn de kreittonos oregontai, toutʼ estin epouraniou. dio ouk epaischynetai autous ho theos theos epikaleisthai autōn, hētoimasen gar autois polin.

paragraphs.text: By faith Abraham, being tried, offered up Isaac: yea, he that had gladly received the promises was offering up his only begotten [son];
paragraphs.original: Πίστει προσενήνοχεν Ἀβραὰμ τὸν Ἰσαὰκ πειραζόμενος, καὶ τὸν μονογενῆ προσέφερεν ὁ τὰς ἐπαγγελίας ἀναδεξάμενος,
paragraphs.translit: Pistei prosenēnochen Abraam ton Isaak peirazomenos, kai ton monogenē prosepheren ho tas epangelias anadexamenos,

paragraphs.text: even he to whom it was said, In Isaac shall thy seed be called:
paragraphs.original: πρὸς ὃν ἐλαλήθη ὅτι Ἐν Ἰσαὰκ κληθήσεταί σοι σπέρμα,
paragraphs.translit: pros hon elalēthē hoti En Isaak klēthēsetai soi sperma,

paragraphs.text: accounting that God [is] able to raise up, even from the dead; from whence he did also in a figure receive him back.
paragraphs.original: λογισάμενος ὅτι καὶ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἐγείρειν δυνατὸς ὁ θεός· ὅθεν αὐτὸν καὶ ἐν παραβολῇ ἐκομίσατο.
paragraphs.translit: logisamenos hoti kai ek nekrōn egeirein dynatos ho theos· hothen auton kai en parabolē ekomisato.

paragraphs.text: By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau, even concerning things to come.
paragraphs.original: Πίστει καὶ περὶ μελλόντων εὐλόγησεν Ἰσαὰκ τὸν Ἰακὼβ καὶ τὸν Ἠσαῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Pistei kai peri mellontōn eulogēsen Isaak ton Iakōb kai ton Ēsau.

paragraphs.text: By faith Jacob, when he was dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph; and worshipped, [leaning] upon the top of his staff.
paragraphs.original: πίστει Ἰακὼβ ἀποθνῄσκων ἕκαστον τῶν υἱῶν Ἰωσὴφ εὐλόγησεν, καὶ προσεκύνησεν ἐπὶ τὸ ἄκρον τῆς ῥάβδου αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: pistei Iakōb apothnēskōn hekaston tōn hyiōn Iōsēph eulogēsen, kai prosekynēsen epi to akron tēs rhabdou autou.

paragraphs.text: By faith Joseph, when his end was nigh, made mention of the departure of the children of Israel; and gave commandment concerning his bones.
paragraphs.original: πίστει Ἰωσὴφ τελευτῶν περὶ τῆς ἐξόδου τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ ἐμνημόνευσεν, καὶ περὶ τῶν ὀστέων αὐτοῦ ἐνετείλατο.
paragraphs.translit: pistei Iōsēph teleutōn peri tēs exodou tōn hyiōn Israēl emnēmoneusen, kai peri tōn osteōn autou eneteilato.

paragraphs.text: By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months by his parents, because they saw he was a goodly child; and they were not afraid of the king`s commandment.
paragraphs.original: Πίστει Μωϋσῆς γεννηθεὶς ἐκρύβη τρίμηνον ὑπὸ τῶν πατέρων αὐτοῦ, διότι εἶδον ἀστεῖον τὸ παιδίον καὶ οὐκ ἐφοβήθησαν τὸ διάταγμα τοῦ βασιλέως.
paragraphs.translit: Pistei Mōysēs gennētheis ekrybē trimēnon hypo tōn paterōn autou, dioti eidon asteion to paidion kai ouk ephobēthēsan to diatagma tou basileōs.

paragraphs.text: By faith Moses, when he was grown up, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh`s daughter;
paragraphs.original: πίστει Μωϋσῆς μέγας γενόμενος ἠρνήσατο λέγεσθαι υἱὸς θυγατρὸς Φαραώ,
paragraphs.translit: pistei Mōysēs megas genomenos ērnēsato legesthai hyios thygatros Pharaō,

paragraphs.text: choosing rather to share ill treatment with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season;
paragraphs.original: μᾶλλον ἑλόμενος συγκακουχεῖσθαι τῷ λαῷ τοῦ θεοῦ ἢ πρόσκαιρον ἔχειν ἁμαρτίας ἀπόλαυσιν,
paragraphs.translit: mallon helomenos synkakoucheisthai tō laō tou theou ē proskairon echein hamartias apolausin,

paragraphs.text: accounting the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures of Egypt: for he looked unto the recompense of reward.
paragraphs.original: μείζονα πλοῦτον ἡγησάμενος τῶν Αἰγύπτου θησαυρῶν τὸν ὀνειδισμὸν τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἀπέβλεπεν γὰρ εἰς τὴν μισθαποδοσίαν.
paragraphs.translit: meizona plouton hēgēsamenos tōn Aigyptou thēsaurōn ton oneidismon tou Christou, apeblepen gar eis tēn misthapodosian.

paragraphs.text: By faith he forsook Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king: for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible.
paragraphs.original: πίστει κατέλιπεν Αἴγυπτον, μὴ φοβηθεὶς τὸν θυμὸν τοῦ βασιλέως, τὸν γὰρ ἀόρατον ὡς ὁρῶν ἐκαρτέρησεν.
paragraphs.translit: pistei katelipen Aigypton, mē phobētheis ton thymon tou basileōs, ton gar aoraton hōs horōn ekarterēsen.

paragraphs.text: By faith he kept the passover, and the sprinkling of the blood, that the destroyer of the firstborn should not touch them.
paragraphs.original: πίστει πεποίηκεν τὸ πάσχα καὶ τὴν πρόσχυσιν τοῦ αἵματος, ἵνα μὴ ὁ ὀλοθρεύων τὰ πρωτότοκα θίγῃ αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: pistei pepoiēken to pascha kai tēn proschysin tou haimatos, hina mē ho olothreuōn ta prōtotoka thigē autōn.

paragraphs.text: By faith they passed through the Red sea as by dry land: which the Egyptians assaying to do were swallowed up.
paragraphs.original: Πίστει διέβησαν τὴν Ἐρυθρὰν Θάλασσαν ὡς διὰ ξηρᾶς γῆς, ἧς πεῖραν λαβόντες οἱ Αἰγύπτιοι κατεπόθησαν.
paragraphs.translit: Pistei diebēsan tēn Erythran Thalassan hōs dia xēras gēs, hēs peiran labontes hoi Aigyptioi katepothēsan.

paragraphs.text: By faith the walls of Jericho fell down, after they had been compassed about for seven days.
paragraphs.original: πίστει τὰ τείχη Ἰεριχὼ ἔπεσαν κυκλωθέντα ἐπὶ ἑπτὰ ἡμέρας.
paragraphs.translit: pistei ta teichē Ierichō epesan kyklōthenta epi hepta hēmeras.

paragraphs.text: By faith Rahab the harlot perished not with them that were disobedient, having received the spies with peace.
paragraphs.original: πίστει Ῥαὰβ ἡ πόρνη οὐ συναπώλετο τοῖς ἀπειθήσασιν, δεξαμένη τοὺς κατασκόπους μετʼ εἰρήνης.
paragraphs.translit: pistei Rhaab hē pornē ou synapōleto tois apeithēsasin, dexamenē tous kataskopous metʼ eirēnēs.

paragraphs.text: And what shall I more say? for the time will fail me if I tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah; of David and Samuel and the prophets:
paragraphs.original: Καὶ τί ἔτι λέγω; ἐπιλείψει με γὰρ διηγούμενον ὁ χρόνος περὶ Γεδεών, Βαράκ, Σαμψών, Ἰεφθάε, Δαυίδ τε καὶ Σαμουὴλ καὶ τῶν προφητῶν,
paragraphs.translit: Kai ti eti legō; epileipsei me gar diēgoumenon ho chronos peri Gedeōn, Barak, Sampsōn, Iephthae, Dauid te kai Samouēl kai tōn prophētōn,

paragraphs.text: who through faith subdued kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions,
paragraphs.original: οἳ διὰ πίστεως κατηγωνίσαντο βασιλείας, εἰργάσαντο δικαιοσύνην, ἐπέτυχον ἐπαγγελιῶν, ἔφραξαν στόματα λεόντων,
paragraphs.translit: hoi dia pisteōs katēgōnisanto basileias, eirgasanto dikaiosynēn, epetychon epangeliōn, ephraxan stomata leontōn,

paragraphs.text: quenched the power of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, from weakness were made strong, waxed mighty in war, turned to flight armies of aliens.
paragraphs.original: ἔσβεσαν δύναμιν πυρός, ἔφυγον στόματα μαχαίρης, ἐδυναμώθησαν ἀπὸ ἀσθενείας, ἐγενήθησαν ἰσχυροὶ ἐν πολέμῳ, παρεμβολὰς ἔκλιναν ἀλλοτρίων·
paragraphs.translit: esbesan dynamin pyros, ephygon stomata machairēs, edynamōthēsan apo astheneias, egenēthēsan ischyroi en polemō, parembolas eklinan allotriōn·

paragraphs.text: Women received their dead by a resurrection: and others were tortured, not accepting their deliverance; that they might obtain a better resurrection:
paragraphs.original: ἔλαβον γυναῖκες ἐξ ἀναστάσεως τοὺς νεκροὺς αὐτῶν· ἄλλοι δὲ ἐτυμπανίσθησαν, οὐ προσδεξάμενοι τὴν ἀπολύτρωσιν, ἵνα κρείττονος ἀναστάσεως τύχωσιν·
paragraphs.translit: elabon gynaikes ex anastaseōs tous nekrous autōn· alloi de etympanisthēsan, ou prosdexamenoi tēn apolytrōsin, hina kreittonos anastaseōs tychōsin·

paragraphs.text: and others had trial of mockings and scourgings, yea, moreover of bonds and imprisonment:
paragraphs.original: ἕτεροι δὲ ἐμπαιγμῶν καὶ μαστίγων πεῖραν ἔλαβον, ἔτι δὲ δεσμῶν καὶ φυλακῆς·
paragraphs.translit: heteroi de empaigmōn kai mastigōn peiran elabon, eti de desmōn kai phylakēs·

paragraphs.text: they were stoned, they were sawn asunder, they were tempted, they were slain with the sword: they went about in sheepskins, in goatskins; being destitute, afflicted, ill-treated
paragraphs.original: ἐλιθάσθησαν, ἐπρίσθησαν, ἐν φόνῳ μαχαίρης ἀπέθανον, περιῆλθον ἐν μηλωταῖς, ἐν αἰγείοις δέρμασιν, ὑστερούμενοι, θλιβόμενοι, κακουχούμενοι,
paragraphs.translit: elithasthēsan, epristhēsan, en phonō machairēs apethanon, periēlthon en mēlōtais, en aigeiois dermasin, hysteroumenoi, thlibomenoi, kakouchoumenoi,

paragraphs.text: (of whom the world was not worthy), wandering in deserts and mountains and caves, and the holes of the earth.
paragraphs.original: ὧν οὐκ ἦν ἄξιος ὁ κόσμος ἐπὶ ἐρημίαις πλανώμενοι καὶ ὄρεσι καὶ σπηλαίοις καὶ ταῖς ὀπαῖς τῆς γῆς·
paragraphs.translit: hōn ouk ēn axios ho kosmos epi erēmiais planōmenoi kai oresi kai spēlaiois kai tais opais tēs gēs·

paragraphs.text: And these all, having had witness borne to them through their faith, received not the promise,
paragraphs.original: καὶ πάντες μαρτυρηθέντες διὰ τῆς πίστεως οὐκ ἐκομίσαντο τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν,
paragraphs.translit: kai pantes martyrēthentes dia tēs pisteōs ouk ekomisanto tēn epangelian,

paragraphs.text: God having provided some better thing concerning us, that apart from us they should not be made perfect.
paragraphs.original: τοῦ θεοῦ περὶ ἡμῶν κρεῖττόν τι προβλεψαμένου, ἵνα μὴ χωρὶς ἡμῶν τελειωθῶσιν.
paragraphs.translit: tou theou peri hēmōn kreitton ti problepsamenou, hina mē chōris hēmōn teleiōthōsin.
